Architecture view of the same finding: the flag ties two separate concerns together. Station budgets are a spend partition (R1 to R3). Completeness is an artifact and verdict precondition (R4). The spec defines R4 independently of partitions, and nothing about completeness depends on a token cap. Making it depend on budget configuration means one fact (is review allowed) is controlled by an unrelated setting. Decision 0014 records the scoping and its trade-off, which is the right practice. But a decision record cannot narrow an accepted spec requirement. The spec ranks above project decisions, so the spec has to be amended, or the coupling removed.

The conflict is real, and the line cannot resolve it. The owner ruling needed is one of two. (1) Amend R4 and S4/S5/S8 to scope completeness to projects that configure efficiency partitions, so decision 0014 matches the spec. (2) Authorize updates to the 22 protected tests and make the precondition unconditional. That is a one-line change at anvil/runner.py:1652. Option 2 gives the cleaner boundary. Option 1 is acceptable if the owner prefers backward compatibility, and the spec should then say so.
